Learning without a model

Dynamic programming needs $p(s', r \mid s, a)$, the full rules of the world. Monte Carlo methods need only experience: play whole episodes, note the return that followed each state, and average. A value is an expected return, so the average of enough returns is the value.

$p(s', r \mid s, a)$: hidden. The agent sees only states, actions and rewards as they happen.

The random policy on the gridworld from Lesson 30. Each episode starts in a random cell and ends in a grey corner. Cells show the average return $V(s)$ and, below it, how many returns were averaged.

How fast do the averages settle?

Worst error $\max_s |V(s) - v_\pi(s)|$ against episodes played so far. It shrinks roughly like $1/\sqrt{n}$.

The maths

By definition (Lesson 21) the value is an expected return:

$$v_\pi(s) = \mathbb{E}_\pi\big[G_t \mid S_t = s\big]$$

Each episode that passes through $s$ supplies one sample of $G_t$. First-visit Monte Carlo keeps, for each state, the returns that followed its first visit in each episode, and averages them:

$$V(s) = \frac{1}{N(s)} \sum_{i=1}^{N(s)} G^{(i)}(s)$$

where $N(s)$ counts those returns. Lesson 6's update keeps this average without storing the list: $V(s) \leftarrow V(s) + \tfrac{1}{N(s)}\big(G - V(s)\big)$.

Here every reward is $-1$ and $\gamma = 1$, so the return from time $t$ is minus the number of steps left:

$$G_t = R_{t+1} + R_{t+2} + \cdots + R_T = -(T - t)$$

The returns of different episodes are independent samples, so by the law of large numbers $V(s) \to v_\pi(s)$ as $N(s) \to \infty$. If the returns from $s$ have standard deviation $\sigma$, the average has standard error

$$\text{SE} = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{N(s)}}$$

so four times as many episodes halve the error. Nothing above uses $p$. The price: an update waits for the episode to end, and the estimates are noisy.

No state's estimate is computed from any other state's estimate. Unlike DP, Monte Carlo does not build values from neighbours' values (it does not bootstrap). It can estimate one state's value alone by starting episodes there.
